a
21
b

c

decision.explanation: Expand and apply linearity of expectation: E[(X−2)(X−3)] = E[X²]−5E[X]+6 = 5−5(−2)+6 = 21.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
Expanding out the product inside the expected value, using the properties of the expected value, and substituting in the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[(X-2)(X-3)] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}-5X+6] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]+\text{E}[-5X]+\text{E}[6] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-5\text{E}[X]+6 \\  & =5-5(-2)+6 \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.15$ | $0.25$ | $0.4$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{4}].$
after.worked_solution:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{4}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{4}]={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{4}\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each squared value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{4}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{4}\cdot f(x) \\  & ={0}^{4}\cdot 0.15+{1}^{4}\cdot 0.25+{2}^{4}\cdot 0.4+{3}^{4}\cdot 0.05+{4}^{4}\cdot 0.15 \\  & =0\cdot 0.15+1\cdot 0.25+16\cdot 0.4+81\cdot 0.05+256\cdot 0.15 \\  & =0+0.25+6.4+4.05+38.4 \\  & =49.1.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{12}, & x=0 \\ \frac{1}{3}, & x=1 \\ \frac{1}{4}, & x=2\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{5}].$
after.worked_solution:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{5}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{5}]={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{5}\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each cubed value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{5}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{5}\cdot f(x) \\  & ={0}^{5}\cdot \frac{5}{12}+{1}^{5}\cdot \frac{1}{3}+{2}^{5}\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =0\cdot \frac{5}{12}+1\cdot \frac{1}{3}+32\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =0+\frac{1}{3}+8 \\  & =\frac{25}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{12}, & x=0 \\ \frac{1}{3}, & x=1 \\ \frac{1}{4}, & x=2\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{5}].$
content.worked_solution:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{5}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{5}]={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{5}\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each cubed value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{5}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{5}\cdot f(x) \\  & ={0}^{5}\cdot \frac{5}{12}+{1}^{5}\cdot \frac{1}{3}+{2}^{5}\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =0\cdot \frac{5}{12}+1\cdot \frac{1}{3}+32\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =0+\frac{1}{3}+8 \\  & =\frac{25}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
